pages.text: Concentration Cores aren't only useful for weaponry - instead, they can be used more creatively too. The Litter is one such example. It's a critter that will follow its user around, leaving behind Light Droppings whenever in dark areas. It can also be picked up. An Inhabiting Ritual is required to create it, which needs a block that constantly emits light, 12 Linear and 4 Curved Ritual Blocks.

pages.name: Inhabiting Ritual
pages.text: To trigger the ritual, use the Concentration Core on the chosen light emitting block.

pages.title: Addendum
pages.text: I find it to be such a shame that the majority of rituals are only every passed down through oral tradition. That's the way I learned about most I know of, such as the Inhabiting or the Scorching Ritual. Rituals offer such fascinating insight into some of the inner workings of the Risus. For example, I was under the impression that Concentration Cores simply gathered and focused the memories stored in the Memory Core used to make

them. Yet, once when I was walking through a Swamp, I noticed that my Litter was actively avoiding Frogs. At first, I assumed that the Core I used might have had a Magma Cube's or other insect's memories inside. I made a couple more Litters to test out this theory, and it turned out, all of them were afraid... It could be that the weak Will inside the Concentration Core adapts to its body, and possibly forms instincts based on that. However, I believe it much more likely that the Core

is closer to a conduit that directly links to the Conglomerate Mind behind the Risus. Alternatively, it could be a combination of both ideas. Either way, it proves how Rituals could be the cornerstone puzzle pieces that I can use to one day complete my research - and finally understand it all.
